option_description: Attestation that every administrative/privileged login is gated by multi-factor authentication (not a password alone), enforced via the IdP/SSO directory with no admin-role exclusions or break-glass bypass left enabled.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of the exposure "Weak / non-phishing-resistant admin authentication" (fires when mfa_enforced_for_admin is_false) and of "Compromise / abuse of valid privileged credentials" (also fires when is_false). Without MFA a stolen admin password alone yields a valid session — the primary enabler of credential stuffing and valid-credential abuse.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the IdP/SSO access policy to confirm an MFA requirement is scoped to all admin/privileged roles with no exclusions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Identity-provider / SSO policy shows an MFA requirement scoped to all admin/privileged roles (CIS 6.5: 'Require MFA for all administrative access accounts, where supported, on all enterprise assets'). Absence of such a policy, or admin roles excluded from it, is insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 6 — Access Control Management (6.5)

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the IdP admin console, inspect the Conditional Access / sign-on policy targeting the privileged-role group.
how_to_obtain.navigation: IdP admin console (e.g. Entra ID > Conditional Access, or Okta > Security > Authentication Policies) > policy targeting the privileged-role group
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A sign-on/Conditional-Access policy requiring MFA targets the privileged-role group with no exclusions; enforcing MFA via the directory/SSO provider satisfies the safeguard.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 6 — Access Control Management (6.3/6.5)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt a password-only admin login to confirm it is rejected and MFA is prompted.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin login portal > sign in with a valid admin password
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The password-only login is rejected / a second factor is demanded before a session is granted; a successful password-only login indicates MFA is not enforced.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether the admin MFA factor is phishing-resistant (FIDO2/WebAuthn or PKI/PIV, origin-bound, AAL2/AAL3) rather than a phishable shared-secret factor (SMS, voice, TOTP, push).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Weak / non-phishing-resistant admin authentication" and of "Compromise / abuse of valid privileged credentials" — both fire when phishing_resistant_authenticator_required eq "sms_otp_or_push". The insecure value lets an AiTM proxy relay the captured OTP/push approval to mint a valid session.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the authenticator policy for privileged accounts to confirm only phishing-resistant factors are permitted.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Authenticator policy for privileged accounts permits only FIDO/WebAuthn or PKI (PIV/CAC); SMS, voice, TOTP, and push are disabled or downgraded for admin roles. Only FIDO/WebAuthn and PKI qualify as phishing-resistant per CISA.
how_to_obtain.source: CISA Implementing Phishing-Resistant MFA fact sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm admin authentication is mapped to AAL2/AAL3 with an origin-bound, verifier-impersonation-resistant authenticator.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Admin authentication is mapped to AAL2/AAL3 with a phishing-resistant (origin-bound, verifier-impersonation-resistant) authenticator per NIST SP 800-63B; password-only or shared-secret OTP for admins is insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-63B Rev 4 — Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication

option_description: Whether the residual password factor for admin accounts is strong, unique, screened against breached-password datasets, with lockout/throttling bound to the account.
security_impact: A secondary OR-trigger of both "Weak / non-phishing-resistant admin authentication" and "Compromise / abuse of valid privileged credentials" — fires when admin_credential_hygiene is_false. Reused/short/breached admin passwords make the password leg stuffable even where MFA exists.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the admin password policy for uniqueness and minimum length requirements.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Unique passwords for all enterprise assets; at minimum 8 chars when paired with MFA, 14 chars without MFA (CIS 5.2). Reused or short admin passwords are insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 5 — Account Management (5.2)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm new/changed admin passwords are screened against breached-password datasets and that per-account lockout/throttling is in place.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: New/changed admin passwords are screened against breached-password datasets (Pwned Passwords) and account lockout/throttling is bound to the account; MFA remains the primary defense against credential stuffing (~99.9% of account-takeover stopped).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Credential Stuffing Prevention Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attestation that every privileged action is attributable to one named human operator — no shared/generic admin logins in routine use.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Compromise / abuse of valid privileged credentials" and of "Non-attributable / unlogged privileged actions" — both fire when no_shared_privileged_credentials is_false. A shared credential broadens who can present 'valid' credentials and makes privileged actions non-attributable even when a log exists.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the account inventory to confirm one privileged identity per operator and no generic/shared admin login in routine human use.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Account inventory (CIS 5.1, covering both user and administrator accounts) shows one privileged identity per operator; no generic/shared admin account is in routine human use. A shared credential means actions are non-attributable.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 5 — Account Management (5.1)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm privileged accounts are administered under a role/attribute scheme with monitored role assignments, and any breakglass accounts are vaulted and individually checked out.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Privileged user accounts are established/administered under a role- or attribute-based scheme with monitored role assignments (AC-2(7)); breakglass/shared accounts, if any, are vaulted, individually checked-out, and session-recorded rather than statically shared.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-2(7) Privileged User Accounts

option_description: Attestation that privileged accounts are monitored for atypical usage (off-hours login, impossible travel, atypical resource access) so abuse of valid admin credentials is detected.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Compromise / abuse of valid privileged credentials" — fires when privileged_session_anomaly_monitoring is_false. Without it an adversary using stolen valid credentials blends into normal traffic undetected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm privileged/system accounts are monitored for atypical usage and that atypical events are reported to defined personnel.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: System accounts are monitored for atypical usage and atypical events are reported to defined personnel (AC-2(12)); privileged-role/attribute changes are monitored (AC-2(7)). No behavioral monitoring on admin accounts is insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-2(12) Account Monitoring for Atypical Usage

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify alerting exists for valid-account abuse patterns and that coverage extends to all admin accounts.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Alerting exists for valid-account abuse patterns (off-hours admin login, impossible travel, privileged access to resources the operator does not normally touch) — the documented detection for T1078 Valid Accounts.
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1078 Valid Accounts

option_description: Attestation that privileged access is just-in-time (requested, justified, approved, time-bounded, auto-revoked) toward Zero Standing Privileges, rather than standing/always-on admin role assignments.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Standing / over-broad privilege exploited for lateral movement" — fires when no_standing_admin_privileges_jit_required is_false. Always-on standing admin rights are something an attacker can ride for lateral movement after a single foothold.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm privileged elevation is brokered just-in-time toward Zero Standing Privileges with no persistent always-on privileged role.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Privileged elevation is brokered just-in-time toward Zero Standing Privileges: each elevation is requested, justified, approved, time-bounded, and automatically revoked; no persistent always-on privileged role assignment. Standing admin = the antidote pattern is absent.
how_to_obtain.source: BeyondTrust — Zero Standing Privileges (ZSP) glossary

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the PAM/PIM tool, confirm privileged roles are assigned as 'eligible' rather than 'active', requiring activation with justification and expiry.
how_to_obtain.navigation: PAM / PIM tool (e.g. Entra PIM > Roles, or CyberArk) > privileged role assignments
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Privileged roles are 'eligible' rather than 'active', requiring activation with justification and an expiry; permanently active privileged assignments are the insecure state.
how_to_obtain.source: BeyondTrust — Zero Standing Privileges (ZSP) glossary

option_description: Attestation that each admin holds only the minimum privileges required for their role via documented RBAC, rather than blanket global-admin / root-everywhere.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Standing / over-broad privilege exploited for lateral movement" — fires when least_privilege_admin_scoping is_false. Over-broad superuser scope lets a compromised operator pivot across the whole trust zone.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review documented RBAC and confirm operators are assigned scoped roles rather than blanket superuser.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented role-based access control defines the access rights necessary for each role (CIS 6.8); operators are assigned scoped roles, not blanket superuser. Global-admin granted by default to all operators is insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 6 — Access Control Management (6.8)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm least privilege is enforced and privileged accounts are restricted to defined personnel/roles.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Least privilege (AC-6) is enforced: each privileged user is authorized only the accesses necessary for assigned tasks, and privileged accounts are restricted to defined personnel/roles (AC-6(5)).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-6 Least Privilege / AC-6(5) Privileged Accounts

option_description: Attestation that privileged access is brokered through a PAM/bastion that vaults credentials and records sessions, so operators do not hold raw long-lived secrets and access is centrally monitored.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Standing / over-broad privilege exploited for lateral movement" and of "Shared / un-vaulted privileged credentials" — both fire when privileged_access_via_pam_with_session_recording is_false. Without the broker, operators connect directly with raw credentials and sessions are unvaulted/unrecorded, widening the lateral-movement surface.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm privileged sessions traverse a PAM/jump-host that vaults credentials and records sessions, and that operators hold no long-lived raw secrets.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Privileged sessions traverse a PAM/jump-host that vaults credentials and records sessions; operators do not hold long-lived raw secrets. AC-2(7) requires privileged accounts be administered and monitored centrally.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-2(7) Privileged User Accounts

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the SSH/admin entry point is a hardened bastion and that direct operator SSH to internal hosts bypassing it is blocked.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SSH/admin entry point is a hardened bastion: password auth and root login disabled, public-key (Ed25519/RSA>=3072) required, internal hosts reachable only from the bastion, keys inventoried and rotated. Direct operator SSH to internal hosts bypassing the bastion is insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: OpenSSH bastion / jump host hardening practice (Teleport)

option_description: Attestation that privileged entitlements are reviewed on a defined recurring frequency and excess/stale rights are reassigned or removed.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Privilege creep / dormant admin accounts" — fires when periodic_privilege_recertification is_false. Without recurring review, entitlements accumulate as unreviewed standing access (privilege creep).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm privileges assigned to roles/classes are reviewed on a defined frequency and reassigned/removed where no longer justified.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Privileges assigned to defined roles/classes are reviewed on a defined frequency and reassigned/removed where no longer justified (AC-6(7)). No recurring privilege review = accumulated standing access.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-6(7) Review of User Privileges

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify an inventory of all user and administrator accounts is maintained and used to drive recertification.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An inventory of all user and administrator accounts is maintained (CIS 5.1) and used to drive recertification; orphaned or unreviewed admin accounts surface as gaps.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 5 — Account Management (5.1)

option_description: Attestation that unused/dormant privileged accounts are disabled or removed within a defined window and that admin access is revoked promptly on termination/role change.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Privilege creep / dormant admin accounts" — fires when dormant_admin_accounts_disabled is_false. Terminated or role-changed operators retain admin access and dormant privileged accounts linger as quiet footholds for re-entry.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm dormant accounts are disabled/deleted after the defined inactivity window and that admin accounts are disabled immediately on termination.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Dormant accounts are deleted/disabled after 45 days of inactivity (CIS 5.3); admin accounts are disabled immediately upon termination (CIS 6.2). Lingering enabled-but-unused admin accounts are insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 5 — Account Management (5.3) / Control 6 (6.2)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify accounts are disabled within a defined period when inactive/expired/orphaned, ideally via automated mechanisms.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Accounts are disabled within a defined period when inactive, expired, or no longer associated with a user (AC-2(3)), ideally via automated mechanisms (AC-2(1)).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-2(3) Disable Accounts / AC-2(1) Automated Account Management

option_description: Insecure-firing attestation: a generic/role 'admin' login is shared by multiple operators in routine human use, so privileged actions are non-attributable. TRUE when such a shared admin credential exists.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Shared / un-vaulted privileged credentials" — fires when shared_admin_accounts is_true (opposite polarity to no_shared_privileged_credentials, which fires is_false). A shared admin credential makes actions non-attributable and broadens who can present valid privileged credentials.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the account inventory for any generic/role admin login shared across operators in routine use.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Account inventory (CIS 5.1, covering both user and administrator accounts) shows one privileged identity per operator; if a generic/shared 'admin' login is in routine human use the attribute is TRUE (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 5 — Account Management (5.1)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm any breakglass/shared account is vaulted and individually checked out rather than statically shared in routine use.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Privileged user accounts are administered under a role/attribute scheme with monitored role assignments (AC-2(7)); breakglass/shared accounts, if any, are vaulted, individually checked-out, and session-recorded — a statically shared admin password sets this attribute TRUE.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-2(7) Privileged User Accounts

option_description: Insecure-firing attestation: operators hold raw, long-lived privileged secrets (static passwords, persistent SSH keys, API tokens) outside a vault rather than checking out short-lived brokered credentials. TRUE when such secrets are held.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Shared / un-vaulted privileged credentials" — fires when operators_hold_raw_longlived_admin_secrets is_true. Raw long-lived privileged secrets outside a vault multiply the credential-theft surface (the un-vaulted half of this vector).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Determine whether operators retain raw long-lived privileged secrets outside a vault rather than checking out short-lived brokered credentials.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Privileged sessions traverse a PAM/jump-host that vaults credentials; operators do not hold long-lived raw secrets (AC-2(7) requires privileged accounts be administered and monitored centrally). Operators retaining static passwords, persistent SSH keys, or API tokens outside a vault sets this attribute TRUE.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-2(7) Privileged User Accounts

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify privileged SSH keys are inventoried, rotated, and not held statically by operators on general-purpose endpoints.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Public-key access is brokered through a hardened bastion with keys inventoried and rotated; long-lived operator-held private keys/tokens that bypass the broker set this attribute TRUE (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OpenSSH bastion / jump host hardening practice (Teleport)

option_description: Attestation that the admin/management network path (admin console, SSH/RDP, control-plane API) is reachable only from internal/trusted networks rather than directly from the public internet.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Internet-exposed admin / management interface" — fires when control_plane_api_not_publicly_exposed is_false. An internet-exposed management plane is an External Remote Services (T1133) initial-access surface frequently entered with valid creds and no exploit signature.

how_to_obtain.instruction: From an external vantage point, confirm management/admin endpoints are unreachable directly from the internet.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Management/admin endpoints (console, SSH, RDP, API control plane) are reachable only from internal networks / via VPN or ZTNA, not directly from the internet; an internet-exposed admin interface is an external-remote-services initial-access surface (T1133).
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1133 External Remote Services

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review network/firewall rules to confirm remote admin access requires MFA and no unauthenticated or single-factor remote management path exists.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Remote admin access requires MFA on all remote network access (CIS 6.4); unauthenticated or single-factor remote management is insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 6 — Access Control Management (6.4)

option_description: Attestation that all remote administrative/management network access (VPN, ZTNA, bastion, direct console) is gated by multi-factor authentication.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Internet-exposed admin / management interface" — fires when remote_admin_access_requires_mfa is_false. Single-factor or unauthenticated remote management means a reachable management plane can be entered with valid creds alone.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm every remote management entry path enforces MFA; reject any path accepting single-factor or unauthenticated access.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Remote admin access requires MFA on all remote network access (CIS 6.4); unauthenticated or single-factor remote management is insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 6 — Access Control Management (6.4)

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the VPN/ZTNA/bastion access policy, verify MFA is required for all remote admin entry paths and attempt a single-factor connect to confirm it is rejected.
how_to_obtain.navigation: VPN/ZTNA/bastion admin console > remote-access authentication policy
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Every remote management entry path (VPN, ZTNA, bastion, direct console) enforces MFA; a single-factor connect attempt is rejected. Any remote admin path accepting single-factor/unauthenticated access is insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Attestation that operators reach the control plane only through a brokered access path (ZTNA or an MFA-gated VPN/bastion) rather than connecting directly to an internet-facing management endpoint.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Internet-exposed admin / management interface" — fires when remote_access_via_ztna_or_mfa_vpn is_false. A direct internet-to-control-plane path bypasses a brokered, identity-aware ingress (T1133).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the only ingress path to the control plane is a brokered, identity-aware channel (ZTNA or MFA-gated VPN/bastion) and that no direct internet-to-management connection succeeds.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Management/admin endpoints are reachable only via VPN or ZTNA, not directly from the internet; a direct internet-to-management connection that bypasses the brokered channel is an external-remote-services initial-access surface (T1133) and is insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1133 External Remote Services

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the remote-access architecture to confirm ZTNA / MFA-gated VPN is the sole sanctioned ingress and direct management exposure is prohibited.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Remote admin access requires MFA on all remote network access (CIS 6.4) routed through a brokered ingress; any direct internet-to-management path is insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 6 — Access Control Management (6.4)

option_description: Attestation that all privileged actions are logged to a centralized, tamper-resistant store (admins cannot modify or delete their own audit trail) with sufficient detail for forensic reconstruction.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Non-attributable / unlogged privileged actions" — fires when audit_log_tamper_evident is_false. Missing or admin-modifiable audit logs make malicious privileged actions undetectable and unreconstructable.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm execution of privileged functions is logged and admin actions appear in the audit trail attributable to a named identity.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Execution of privileged functions is logged (AC-6(9)); admin actions appear in the audit trail attributable to a named identity. Privileged actions that produce no audit record are insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-6(9) Log Use of Privileged Functions

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify logs are centrally collected and protected from modification (append-only/WORM or separate-account forwarding), covering all root/administrator actions and access to audit logs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Per PCI DSS Req 10.2, all individual access to sensitive data, all root/administrator actions, and access to audit logs are logged; logs are centrally collected and protected from modification (CIS 8.2/8.3). Admin-modifiable or local-only logs are insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 10 — Log and Monitor All Access
